question: What is the primary goal of time management in nursing?

options.A: Ensuring patient safety and care quality
options.C: Reducing the number of nursing shifts

explanation: Organizing clinical tasks deliberately helps protect patients from errors and maintains high standards of care. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is structured time allocation particularly important in Nigerian clinical settings?

options.A: Electronic health records require constant typing
options.B: Hospital policies forbid overtime work completely
options.C: High patient-to-nurse ratios demand careful organization
options.D: Patients refuse care if nurses are slow

explanation: Heavy workloads and staff shortages mean nurses must manage limited time efficiently to cover all essential duties. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h1)

question: The first step in managing shift time effectively is what?
explanation: Reviewing patient needs and ward requirements at the start of the shift sets a clear foundation for planning. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why must a nurse remain flexible with a daily work schedule?

options.A: Ward managers change hospital rules frequently
options.C: Patients sleep through scheduled medication rounds
options.D: Sudden patient emergencies disrupt planned routines

explanation: Clinical environments are unpredictable, requiring nurses to adjust their plans when urgent situations arise. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does the 'A' stand for in the ABCDE prioritization framework?
explanation: Airway management is always the very first priority in patient resuscitation and emergency assessment. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h3)

question: A nurse receives four requests at once. Which task should be handled first?

options.A: A postoperative patient suddenly gasping for breath
options.B: A stable patient asking for a cup of water
options.C: A routine 10:00 AM blood pressure check on a stable ward
options.D: A family member requesting a discharge receipt

explanation: Breathing difficulties threaten life immediately, placing this task in the urgent and important category above all others. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is a major clinical risk associated with frequent workplace interruptions?
explanation: Getting distracted while preparing or giving medications often leads to mistakes in dosage or drug selection. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why does searching for missing medical equipment waste valuable shift time?

options.A: It automatically lowers the nurse's monthly salary
options.B: It forces doctors to cancel all surgical procedures
options.C: It breaks hospital accreditation standards instantly
options.D: It pulls the nurse away from direct patient monitoring

explanation: Spending time looking for supplies delays patient care and disrupts the planned flow of the shift. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h4)

question: Who retains ultimate accountability after a nursing task is delegated?

options.B: The junior staff member who performed the task
options.C: The registered nurse who delegated the task

explanation: Even when a task is handed over, the registered nurse remains legally and professionally responsible for the overall outcome. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which task is most appropriate to delegate to a trained healthcare assistant?

options.A: Conducting a formal patient admission assessment
options.B: Recording routine vital signs for a stable patient
options.D: Developing a complex nursing care plan

explanation: Routine observations on stable individuals fit the skill level of support staff, freeing up the nurse for complex duties. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary benefit of using a pocket notebook or task sheet during a shift?

options.A: Speeding up the doctor's ward round process
options.B: Preventing mental overload and forgotten tasks
options.C: Eliminating the need for verbal handovers

explanation: External tracking tools free up mental space, ensuring that no scheduled treatments or patient requests slip through the cracks. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h6)

question: When is the best time to write down new tasks that arise during a busy shift?

options.A: At the end of the working week
options.C: Only during the final handover meeting
options.D: When the patient complains of pain

explanation: Jotting down tasks right away prevents them from being forgotten amidst the constant distractions of the ward. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h6)

question: How are duties managed effectively during a sudden hospital ward emergency?

options.A: Specific roles are assigned to team members
options.B: Staff wait until the shift supervisor arrives
options.C: One nurse handles every single procedure alone
options.D: All documentation is completed before acting

explanation: Assigning distinct responsibilities like compressions or medications ensures efficient teamwork during high-stress crises. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why is role clarity crucial when responding to a cardiac arrest in a clinical unit?

options.A: It ensures junior nurses do not speak to doctors
options.B: It reduces the cost of emergency medications
options.C: It prevents confusion and wasted time during resuscitation
options.D: It stops family members from entering the ward

explanation: Clear role division eliminates overlapping efforts and speeds up life-saving interventions when every second counts. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is a common psychological consequence of chronic poor time management in nursing?
explanation: Constantly feeling rushed and disorganized leads to high stress levels and eventual emotional and physical exhaustion. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why is end-of-shift reflection important for professional growth?

options.A: It proves to management that overtime is unnecessary
options.B: It replaces the formal hospital incident reporting system
options.C: It allows nurses to leave the hospital premises early
options.D: It helps identify workflow bottlenecks to improve future shifts

explanation: Reviewing what caused delays allows nurses to adjust their planning strategies and work more efficiently tomorrow. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h8)
